reason: The quoted call is verbatim and genuinely lacks ATOMIC_MOVE: on Windows JDK 21 sun/nio/fs/WindowsFileCopy.move deletes the existing target (DeleteFile at line 390) before MoveFileEx(source,target,0) at line 410, so a rename failure leaves statsFile gone and the finally at StatsManager.java:474-478 then deletes the complete tmp file. The impact is overstated, however: the catch at :467-472 sets dirty = true, so the next 60-second flush (or saveNow) rebuilds the whole snapshot from the in-memory cache and rewrites the file, making the loss self-healing within one flush cycle in the ordinary failure case. A process crash between the delete and the rename does not run the finally at all, so the full tmp file survives on disk; only a failed rename during the final shutdown saveNow (HilltopVillagePlugin.java:316-322) can turn the window into permanent loss. The code therefore has a real non-atomic replace and a risky tmp cleanup, but it is a narrow single-flush window, not 'all statistics lost outright'.
